name: Erastus
title: Paul's coworker and servant
summary: Erastus was one of Paul's faithful coworkers in the early church. He was sent together with Timothy to Macedonia to serve the congregations there, while Paul himself remained in Asia for a time. He is also mentioned in connection with his travels and service in the early Christian mission.

keyEvents.title: Sent to Macedonia with Timothy
keyEvents.description: Paul sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he himself remained in Asia a little longer.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Paul's second letter to Timothy
keyEvents.description: In his second letter to Timothy, Paul mentions that Erastus stayed behind in Corinth, showing his continued service and connection to the congregations.

keyEvents.title: Possible identification as city treasurer in Corinth
keyEvents.description: In Romans, an Erastus who is the city's treasurer (steward) sends his greetings. Many scholars believe this may be the same person, which would show his prominent position in society.

keyEvents.title: Service during the riot in Ephesus
keyEvents.description: Erastus was sent away shortly before the silversmith Demetrius caused a riot in Ephesus because of Paul's preaching, which threatened the idol worship of Artemis.
